title: 14  Glossary
text:
Term
Definition
Examples from this document




Cross-reference (xref) or membership table
A table summarising assessments of fuzzy membership of units in a source classification to units in a target classification.
membership_tbl; see Chapter 5 and Chapter 15.


Lookup table (lookup_tbl)
Controlled vocabulary listing all valid unit IDs, names, and conceptual eligibility flags (eligible = TRUE/FALSE) for a source or target classification.
TASVEG and IUCN_GET; see Chapter 4.


Source
The classification being cross-referenced from.
TASVEG 5.0, Tasmania’s vegetation classification and map; see Chapter 2.


Source unit
One ecological concept or mapping unit of the source classification, assessed independently.
Vegetation communities in TASVEG 5.0; see Chapter 2.


Source unit id / Source id
Unique identifier for each unit in the source classification.
VEGCODE column in the TASVEG lookup table (Chapter 4).


Target
The classification being cross-referenced to.
IUCN Global Ecosystem Typology (IUCN GET); see Chapter 3.


Target unit
One unit of the target classification.
Level 3 Ecosystem Functional Groups (EFGs) of IUCN GET; see Chapter 3.


Target unit id / Target id
Unique identifier for each target unit.
EFG or efg_id columns (realm + biome + group, e.g. T2.6 terrestrial, F2.2 freshwater, MT2.1 marine–terrestrial, TF1.7 terrestrial–freshwater wetland, MFT1.3 marine–freshwater–terrestrial).


Interpreter
A domain expert who provides fuzzy membership assessments during elicitation.
Referred to as interpreter or expert interchangeably (AK, AL, DAK, JB, MGT); see Chapter 5.


Membership
An interpreter’s fuzzy estimate (Zadeh 1965) of the relationship between a source unit and a target unit on \([0, 1]\), where 0 means excluded and 1 means unambiguous membership.
memb column; see Chapter 5 and Chapter 15.


Assigned / not assigned
Targets given positive membership (\(> 0\)) by an interpreter are assigned (summing to 1 per source unit). Other candidate targets not listed by that interpreter for an assessed unit are not assigned (implicit membership 0).
See Chapter 5 and Chapter 8.


Not assessed
The interpreter provided no record for the source unit in that round; kept as NA in membership_matrix and never filled with 0.
E.g. 55 units not assessed by Jayne_Balmer in Round 1 (Chapter 8).


Record
One interpreter’s membership estimate for one (source, target, round) combination (one row in long format).
See Chapter 5.


Profile
An interpreter’s full membership vector for one source unit across all candidate targets considered for that unit.
Used in calc_agreement() and calc_shannons_entropy().


Membership matrix
3D numeric array [source, target, interpreter] produced by ecoSynthesis::membership_matrix(), with 0 for unused targets and NA for unassessed units.
TASVEG_mtx_r1, TASVEG_mtx_r2; see Chapter 8 and Chapter 15.


Dissimilarity
Half-\(L_1\) distance between two interpreters’ profiles for a unit: \(D = \frac{1}{2}\sum_k |a_k - b_k|\) (equivalent to Bray–Curtis dissimilarity for unit-sum vectors; 0 = identical, 1 = no overlap).
dissimilarity in calc_agreement(); see Chapter 8.


Agreement / Similarity
Complement of dissimilarity: \(S = 1 - D\) (1 = identical profiles, 0 = no shared target membership).
similarity, mean_similarity in calc_agreement(); see Chapter 8.


Identical
Two profiles with dissimilarity below 0.001.
share_identical in calc_agreement().


Expert pair
Two interpreters compared on the same source unit (6 pairs among 4 interpreters in Round 1; 10 pairs among 5 interpreters in Round 2).
interpreter_x, interpreter_y.


Contested unit
A source unit with high mean pairwise dissimilarity across interpreter pairs.
E.g. FMG, FSM, SWR; see Chapter 8 and Chapter 9.


Shannon’s entropy (normalised)
Information-theoretic measure of within-interpreter fuzziness/ambiguity on \([0, 1]\), normalised by \(\log_2(N)\) under interpreter (\(S\)), source (\(N_{\text{source}}\)), or set (\(N_{\text{set}}\)) bases (Shannon 1948; Pielou 1966).
calc_shannons_entropy(), calc_entropy_tbl(); see Chapter 8–Chapter 10.


Proportion of membership (prop_memb)
Aggregated share of total Round 2 membership votes across interpreters assigned to a target EFG for a source unit.
summarise_membership(); see Chapter 11.


Supporting interpreters (supporting)
Number of interpreters (out of total_interp) who assigned positive membership (\(> 0\)) to a candidate EFG for a source unit.
summarise_membership(); see Chapter 11 and Chapter 13.


Data checks
Non-destructive validation diagnostics checking numeric type, missing values, \([0, 1]\) bounds, source eligibility, and target validity.
check_membership(); see Chapter 6.

title: 15  Membership data formats
text:
15.1 Membership matrix
The diagram below illustrates a minimal cross-referencing example consisting of two classifications with two concepts each, linked by fuzzy membership values (Zadeh 1965; IUCN 2025).
These relationships can be represented in three main tabular formats, each suited to a different stage of data entry or computation.
A membership matrix places source concepts in rows and target concepts in columns:
The dimensions grow with the product of both classifications (\(n\) rows for the source and \(m\) columns for the target). Matrices expose zero and non-zero memberships transparently and are convenient for spreadsheet entry (used by AK_V1 and AL_V2 in Chapter 5) and numerical distance calculations—in ecoSynthesis, membership_matrix() builds a 3D [source, target, interpreter] array directly from a long-format membership_tbl for calc_agreement(). However, 2D matrices become unwieldy for storing multi-round metadata and sparse large classifications.

All analytical steps and standalone output scripts in this repository are written in R, and this documentation book is rendered with Quarto following FAIR data and research software practices (Wilkinson et al. 2016; Barker et al. 2022).

title: 17  Overview of workflow outputs
text:
17.1 Status summary of workflow outputs
To preserve a clean separation between analytical documentation (this Quarto book in docs-src/) and data-product generation, all computationally intensive spatial outputs are produced by standalone, reproducible R scripts stored in scripts/ and written to dedicated subfolders under results/. Each output package is documented with Frictionless Data Package schemas (datapackage.json), Zenodo deposit metadata (.zenodo.json), and a dynamically rendered README.qmd before deposition on Zenodo.
Figure 17.1 illustrates how TASVEG 5.0 spatial polygons and multi-interpreter membership tables feed into the three core state-level outputs.
The table below summarises the current release status of all core and derived outputs generated by the TASVEG-XREF workflow. Currently, Output 3 (90 m Best-Candidate Spatial Synthesis) is published on Zenodo (under embargo until 2027-06-01), while the remaining core and single-EFG derived outputs are in draft or active development.

text:
17.2 Core state-level outputs

17.2.1 Output 1: Spatial data + membership matrices (In development)
This bundle preserves the full polygon geometry (dissolved by VEGCODE into a GeoPackage) alongside five full-width per-interpreter CSV membership matrices formatted for integration with national-scale cross-referencing collections. Expand the block below to inspect the standalone generation script (scripts/TASVEG-membership-matrices.R):



Workflow for vector bundle and per-interpreter membership matrices

scripts/TASVEG-membership-matrices.R

## The purpose of this script is to create a bundle of spatial vector
## (GeoPackage) and membership matrices for each source to target units
## including all TASVEG 5.0 polygons.
##
## Source classification and spatial data (units):
## > TASVEG 5.0 (vegetation communities)
## Target classification (unit):
## > IUCN Global Ecosystem Typology Level 3
## Output format:
## > GeoPackage (`TASVEG-xref-IUCN-GET.gpkg`) in `results/TASVEG-vector-bundle/`
## > with multiple attribute tables (one for each interpreter),
## > plus companion membership matrices in csv format:
## > (`TASVEG-xref-IUCN-GET-{initials}.csv`)
##
## Recommended usage:
## R --vanilla --file="scripts/TASVEG-membership-matrices.R" > docs-src/reproducibility-notes/TASVEG-membership-matrices-out.txt

## Step 0: Setup

### Benchmarking
start_time <- Sys.time()
date()

### Libraries
library(ecoSynthesis)
library(geco)
library(sf)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(readr)
library(XML)


### Paths
here::i_am("scripts/TASVEG-membership-matrices.R")

## Step 2: Generate 90m membership GeoTIFF per candidate EFG

efg_stats_list <- list()

for (tid in IUCN_GET_LUT$efg_id) {
  cat(sprintf("Starting %s: %s // ", tid, date()))
  fname <- sprintf("TASVEG-xref-%s-memb-%sm.tiff", tid, rez)
  out_file <- here::here(out_dir, fname)

  if (tid %in% TASVEG_summary$EFG) {
    efg_name_str <- IUCN_GET_LUT$efg_name[IUCN_GET_LUT$efg_id == tid][1]

    if (file.exists(out_file)) {
      cat(sprintf("%s already exists, loading for summary\n", fname))
      k_rast <- rast(out_file)
    } else {
      TASVEG_k <- TASVEG |> filter(EFG == tid)
      k_rast <- fasterize(
        TASVEG_k,
        TASVEG_raster,
        field = "prop_memb",
        fun = "sum"
      ) |>
        rast()

      rast_metadata <- c(
        PROJECT = "Ecosystem Indicators Workflows",
        TITLE = sprintf("Aggregated membership for %s (%s)", tid, efg_name_str),
        DESCRIPTION = sprintf(
          "Proportion of total Round 2 membership votes (prop_memb) from TASVEG 5.0 to IUCN GET %s (%s) at %sm resolution",
          tid,
          efg_name_str,
          rez
        ),
        EFG_CODE = tid,
        EFG_NAME = efg_name_str
      )
      metags(k_rast) <- rast_metadata

      writeRaster(k_rast, out_file, overwrite = TRUE)
    }

    vals <- values(k_rast, mat = FALSE)
    valid_vals <- vals[!is.na(vals) & vals > 0]
    sum_memb <- sum(valid_vals)
    n_pixels <- length(valid_vals)
    print(sum_memb)

    efg_stats_list[[tid]] <- tibble(
      EFG = tid,
      file_name = fname,
      mapped_pixels_90m = n_pixels,
      unweighted_area_km2 = round(n_pixels * (rez * rez) / 1e6, 2),
      sum_pixel_memb = round(sum_memb, 3),
      weighted_area_km2 = round(sum_memb * (rez * rez) / 1e6, 2)
    )
  } else {
    cat(sprintf("%s not found\n", tid))
  }
}

## 1. Overview & Methodology

This dataset provides **`r n_efgs` spatial raster layers (`r res_xy[1]` m resolution GeoTIFFs)** representing the aggregated fuzzy membership (`prop_memb`) of Tasmania's statewide vegetation map (**TASVEG 5.0**) to each candidate Level 3 **Ecosystem Functional Group (EFG)** of the **IUCN Global Ecosystem Typology (IUCN GET)**.

### Why Per-EFG Membership Rasters?

When cross-referencing regional vegetation classifications (TASVEG 5.0) to global functional typologies (IUCN GET), individual mapping units (`VEGCODE`) frequently have partial or one-to-many relationships across multiple target EFGs (due to environmental gradients, broad mapping complex definitions, or expert uncertainty).

- Whereas a single **"best-candidate" ("winner-takes-all")** map retains only the single highest-scoring EFG per source unit (`r n_best_efgs` EFGs in Tasmania), this **per-EFG membership raster stack** retains **all `r n_efgs` candidate EFGs** assigned any non-zero membership in Round `r round_nr` across the `r n_interp` interpreters—including **`r n_nonbest_efgs` additional EFGs** that represent secondary/partial ecosystem components within TASVEG mapping units.
- For each source `VEGCODE` $s$ and candidate target EFG $t$, the aggregated membership proportion is calculated across all `r n_interp` interpreters in Round `r round_nr` (`ecoSynthesis::summarise_membership(..., keep_all = TRUE, which_round = 2)`):
  $$\text{prop\_memb}_{s, t} = \frac{\sum_{i=1}^{`r n_interp`} m_{s, t, i}}{\sum_{k} \sum_{i=1}^{`r n_interp`} m_{s, k, i}}$$
- For each EFG $t$, polygons in `TASVEG_5_0.shp` with $\text{prop\_memb}_{s, t} > 0$ are rasterized at **`r res_xy[1]` m × `r res_xy[2]` m** resolution using `fasterize::fasterize(..., field = "prop_memb", fun = "sum")`. Pixels outside polygons assigned to EFG $t$ (as well as the three non-eligible natural units `OAQ`, `ORO`, and `OSM`) are encoded as `NoData` (`NA`).

## 3. Spatial Specifications

All `r n_efgs` GeoTIFF files (`TASVEG-xref-{EFG}-memb-90m.tiff`) share an identical spatial grid:

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| **Coordinate Reference System (CRS)** | ``r crs_label`` |
| **Spatial Resolution** | ``r sprintf("%g m × %g m", res_xy[1], res_xy[2])`` (``r sprintf("%.4f km²", pixel_km2)`` / ``r sprintf("%.2f ha", pixel_ha)`` per pixel) |
| **Grid Dimensions** | ``r sprintf("%d rows × %d columns × %d band", n_rows, n_cols, n_bands)`` (``r format(total_cells, big.mark = ",")`` total grid cells) |
| **Bounding Box (`xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax`)** | ``r sprintf("%.0f, %.0f, %.0f, %.0f", ext_bbox[1], ext_bbox[2], ext_bbox[3], ext_bbox[4])`` (meters, `r paste0(crs_info$authority[1], ":", crs_info$code[1])`) |
| **Pixel Values (`prop_memb`)** | Continuous floating-point values in $(0, 1]$ where EFG membership $>0$; `NA` (`NoData`) elsewhere |
| **Total Weighted Area Across All `r n_efgs` Layers** | ``r sprintf("%s km²", format(round(total_weighted_km2, 2), big.mark = ",", nsmall = 2))`` ($\sum_{t=1}^{`r n_efgs`} \sum_{\text{pixels}} \text{prop\_memb}_{t} \times 0.0081\text{ km}^2$) |
| **Embedded GDAL Metadata Tags** | `AREA_OR_POINT = Area`, `PROJECT`, `TITLE`, `DESCRIPTION`, `EFG_CODE`, `EFG_NAME` |

| `max_supporting` | `integer` | Maximum number of interpreters assigning $>0$ membership to this EFG across its contributing TASVEG units (`1` to ``r n_interp``). |

| `unweighted_area_km2` | `numeric` | Total unweighted area ($\text{km}^2$) of all 90 m cells where `prop_memb > 0`. |
| `sum_pixel_memb` | `numeric` | Sum of `prop_memb` across all 90 m grid cells in the raster. |
| `weighted_area_km2` | `numeric` | Membership-weighted area ($\text{km}^2$), equal to `sum_pixel_memb * 0.0081`. |

## 1. Overview & Methodology

This dataset provides a **`r res_xy[1]` m resolution spatial synthesis** and **tabular cross-reference lookup tables** aligning Tasmania's statewide vegetation map (**TASVEG 5.0**) with Level 3 **Ecosystem Functional Groups (EFGs)** of the **IUCN Global Ecosystem Typology (IUCN GET)**.

### Cross-Referencing & Expert Elicitation Workflow

Following the IUCN standards and guidelines for cross-referencing ecosystem classifications and maps (IUCN, 2025), the workflow proceeded through four stages:

1. **Conceptual Alignment & Eligibility Assessment:**
   - **Source classification:** TASVEG 5.0 (`LIST_TASVEG_50_STATEWIDE`, released November 2025; Kitchener & Harris, 2013), comprising **`r n_total_units` unique mapping units (`VEGCODE`)** in the statewide polygon shapefile across mainland Tasmania and surrounding islands.
   - **Eligibility:** **`r n_eligible_units` mapping units** represent ecological vegetation communities or anthropogenic/modified ecosystems eligible for cross-referencing to the IUCN GET. **`r n_ineligible` mapping units** in the group *Other natural environments* (`r ineligible_list`) represent broad mapping complexes combining multiple distinct ecosystem types or non-vegetated substrates that cannot be unambiguously aligned to a single ecosystem concept without auxiliary spatial data; these `r n_ineligible` units are flagged as `eligible = FALSE` and assigned `NoData` (`NA`) in the spatial rasters. *(Note: Three additional codes present in the TASVEG 5.0 Fire Attributes DBF lookup table—`FPL`, `HUE`, and `SLW`—do not occur as polygons in the statewide shapefile).*
   - **Target classification:** IUCN Global Ecosystem Typology (Keith et al., 2022) at **Level 3: Ecosystem Functional Groups (EFGs)**.

2. **Two-Round Structured Expert Elicitation:**
   - `r n_interp` domain experts (MGT, DAK, AL, AK, JB) independently assessed the fuzzy membership ($0 < \text{memb} \le 1$, summing to $1.0$ per source unit and interpreter) of each eligible TASVEG 5.0 community across candidate IUCN GET EFGs.
   - Discrepancies and contested units from **Round 1** were systematically reviewed in group discussions, after which experts provided revised assessments in **Round `r round_nr`**.

3. **Synthesis ("Best Candidate" / Winner-Takes-All):**
   - Using the validated **Round `r round_nr`** assessments across all **`r n_interp` interpreters**, membership scores were aggregated by `VEGCODE` using `ecoSynthesis::summarise_membership(..., keep_all = FALSE, which_round = 2)`.
   - For each source `VEGCODE`, the candidate EFG receiving the highest **proportion of total membership votes (`prop_memb`)** across the `r n_interp` interpreters was selected as the **best candidate**.
   - Across the `r n_eligible_units` eligible TASVEG 5.0 units, **`r n_efgs` IUCN GET Ecosystem Functional Groups** were selected as best candidates, with `prop_memb` ranging from **`r sprintf("%.2f", prop_min)` to `r sprintf("%.2f", prop_max)`** (median **`r sprintf("%.2f", prop_median)`**, mean **`r sprintf("%.3f", prop_mean)`**). For **`r supp_max_row$n_units` of `r n_eligible_units` units** (`r sprintf("%.1f%%", supp_max_row$pct_area)` of mapped area), all `r supp_max_row$supporting` interpreters assigned non-zero membership to the winning EFG (`supporting = ` `r supp_max_row$supporting`).

4. **Spatial Rasterization (`r res_xy[1]` m GeoTIFFs):**
   - The synthesised table was joined to the TASVEG 5.0 polygon geometries (`TASVEG_5_0.shp`) and rasterized at **`r res_xy[1]` m × `r res_xy[2]` m resolution** in ``r crs_label`` using `fasterize::fasterize()`.
   - Standard integer pixel codes (`efg_pixel_value`) and official hex color tables (`efg_hex_code`) from the Global Ecosystems Atlas (`geco` R package) were embedded into the target GeoTIFF.

---

## 2. File Inventory

| File Name | Format | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `TASVEG-xref-target.tiff` | GeoTIFF (`r datatype(r_target)` / integer, embedded color table) | **Best-candidate IUCN GET Ecosystem Functional Group** at `r res_xy[1]` m resolution. Pixel values (``r min(efg_lut$efg_pixel_value)`` to ``r max(efg_lut$efg_pixel_value)``) correspond to `efg_pixel_value` in `IUCN-GET-pixel-lookup.csv`. |
| `TASVEG-xref-membership.tiff` | GeoTIFF (`r datatype(r_memb)` / float32) | **Proportion of total membership votes (`prop_memb`)** supporting the best-candidate EFG in Round `r round_nr` (continuous values from ``r sprintf("%.2f", memb_minmax[1])`` to ``r sprintf("%.2f", memb_minmax[2])``). Quantifies thematic/cross-referencing certainty. |
| `TASVEG-xref-supporting.tiff` | GeoTIFF (`r datatype(r_supp)` / integer) | **Number of supporting interpreters (`supporting`)** out of `r n_interp` who assigned $>0$ membership to the best-candidate EFG in Round `r round_nr` (integer values: `r paste(sprintf("\x60%d\x60", sort(freq_supp$value)), collapse = ", ")`). |
| `TASVEG-xref-best-candidate.csv` | CSV (UTF-8, `r nrow(xref_tbl)` rows) | **Complete TASVEG 5.0 to IUCN GET synthesis table** linking all `r n_total_units` statewide shapefile `VEGCODE` units (``r n_eligible_units`` eligible + ``r n_ineligible`` non-eligible) to their best-candidate EFG, pixel value, color codes, `prop_memb`, and `supporting` counts. |
| `IUCN-GET-pixel-lookup.csv` | CSV (UTF-8, `r nrow(efg_lut)` rows) | **Raster pixel value dictionary** mapping the `r nrow(efg_lut)` integer codes (`efg_pixel_value`: ``r min(efg_lut$efg_pixel_value)``–``r max(efg_lut$efg_pixel_value)``) in `TASVEG-xref-target.tiff` to EFG codes, EFG names, IUCN GET Realm/Biome hierarchy, RGB/Hex colors, and number of TASVEG communities. |
| `TASVEG-xref-target.qml` | QGIS Style XML | **QGIS layer style file** for `TASVEG-xref-target.tiff`. Place in the same folder as the `.tiff` to automatically display official Global Ecosystems Atlas colors and EFG code + name labels in QGIS. |
| `TASVEG-xref-target.clr` | GDAL / ESRI Color Map | **Standard RGBA color map file** (`value R G B A label`) for styling `TASVEG-xref-target.tiff` in ArcGIS, GDAL, or other GIS software. |
| `datapackage.json` | JSON (Frictionless Data) | **Machine-readable Frictionless Data Package specification** describing all tabular schemas, field definitions, and spatial raster metadata. |
| `.zenodo.json` | JSON | **Zenodo deposit metadata** (creators, ORCIDs, affiliations, license, keywords, and related DOIs/URLs). |
| `LICENSE` | Plain text / Markdown | **Full licensing terms** (CC BY 4.0 for data/docs, CC BY 3.0 AU attribution for TASVEG 5.0, MIT for code). |
| `README.md` / `README.qmd` | Markdown / Quarto | **Dataset documentation file** and the reproducible Quarto template that generates it. |

---

## 3. Spatial Specifications

All three GeoTIFF files (`TASVEG-xref-target.tiff`, `TASVEG-xref-membership.tiff`, `TASVEG-xref-supporting.tiff`) share an identical spatial grid:

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| **Coordinate Reference System (CRS)** | ``r crs_label`` |
| **Spatial Resolution** | ``r sprintf("%g m × %g m", res_xy[1], res_xy[2])`` (``r sprintf("%.4f km²", pixel_km2)`` / ``r sprintf("%.2f ha", pixel_ha)`` per pixel) |
| **Grid Dimensions** | ``r sprintf("%d rows × %d columns × %d band", n_rows, n_cols, n_bands)`` (``r format(total_cells, big.mark = ",")`` total grid cells) |
| **Mapped Onshore Pixels** | ``r format(mapped_pixels, big.mark = ",")`` valid pixels (``r sprintf("%s km²", format(round(mapped_area_km2, 2), big.mark = ",", nsmall = 2))`` total mapped area) |
| **NoData (`NA`) Pixels** | ``r format(nodata_pixels, big.mark = ",")`` pixels (marine/background outside TASVEG polygons + non-eligible units `OAQ`, `ORO`, `OSM`) |
| **Bounding Box (`xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax`)** | ``r sprintf("%.0f, %.0f, %.0f, %.0f", ext_bbox[1], ext_bbox[2], ext_bbox[3], ext_bbox[4])`` (meters, `r paste0(crs_info$authority[1], ":", crs_info$code[1])`) |
| **Rasterization Rule (`fasterize`)** | `TASVEG-xref-target.tiff`: `fun = "first"` on `efg_pixel_value`<br>`TASVEG-xref-membership.tiff`: `fun = "max"` on `prop_memb`<br>`TASVEG-xref-supporting.tiff`: `fun = "max"` on `supporting` |
| **Embedded GDAL Metadata Tags** | `AREA_OR_POINT = Area`<br>`PROJECT = Ecosystem Indicators Workflows`<br>`DESCRIPTION = Synthesis of crossreference from TASVEG 5.0 to IUCN GET`<br>`TITLE = <Layer-specific title>` |

---

## 4. Lookup Table: Target Pixel Values (`TASVEG-xref-target.tiff`)

The table below lists all **`r n_efgs` IUCN GET Level 3 Ecosystem Functional Groups** present in `TASVEG-xref-target.tiff` (also provided in machine-readable form in `IUCN-GET-pixel-lookup.csv`):

```{r}
#| label: efg-lookup-table
#| results: asis
tbl_rows <- efg_summary_tbl |>
    transmute(
        `Pixel Value (\`efg_pixel_value\`)` = sprintf("**%d**", efg_pixel_value),
        `EFG Code` = sprintf("`%s`", EFG),
        `Ecosystem Functional Group Name (\`efg_name\`)` = efg_name,
        `Realm (\`realm_id\`)` = sprintf("`%s` (%s)", realm_id, realm_name),
        `Biome (\`biome_id\`)` = sprintf("`%s`", biome_id),
        `Hex Color (\`efg_hex_code\`)` = sprintf("`%s`", efg_hex_code),
        `TASVEG Units (\`n_tasveg_units\`)` = as.character(n_tasveg_units),
        `Mapped Pixels (90 m)` = format(count, big.mark = ","),
        `Mapped Area (km²)` = format(round(area_km2, 2), big.mark = ",", nsmall = 2)
    )

total_row <- tibble(
    `Pixel Value (\`efg_pixel_value\`)` = "**Total**",
    `EFG Code` = "—",
    `Ecosystem Functional Group Name (\`efg_name\`)` = sprintf("**%d Ecosystem Functional Groups**", n_efgs),
    `Realm (\`realm_id\`)` = sprintf("**%d Realms**", n_realms),
    `Biome (\`biome_id\`)` = sprintf("**%d Biomes**", n_biomes),
    `Hex Color (\`efg_hex_code\`)` = "—",
    `TASVEG Units (\`n_tasveg_units\`)` = sprintf("**%d**", sum(efg_summary_tbl$n_tasveg_units)),
    `Mapped Pixels (90 m)` = sprintf("**%s**", format(mapped_pixels, big.mark = ",")),
    `Mapped Area (km²)` = sprintf("**%s**", format(round(mapped_area_km2, 2), big.mark = ",", nsmall = 2))
)

kable(
    bind_rows(tbl_rows, total_row),
    format = "pipe",
    align = c("r", "l", "l", "l", "l", "l", "r", "r", "r")
)
```

### Summary of Uncertainty Layers

- **`TASVEG-xref-membership.tiff` (`prop_memb`)**:
  - Represents the proportion of total membership votes across all `r n_interp` interpreters in Round `r round_nr` assigned to the winning EFG:
    $$\text{prop\_memb}_{s, t^*} = \frac{\sum_{i=1}^{`r n_interp`} m_{s, t^*, i}}{\sum_{t} \sum_{i=1}^{`r n_interp`} m_{s, t, i}}$$
  - Values range from **`r sprintf("%.2f", memb_minmax[1])`** (contested/broadly split source unit) to **`r sprintf("%.2f", memb_minmax[2])`** (unanimous 100% assignment by all `r n_interp` interpreters).
- **`TASVEG-xref-supporting.tiff` (`supporting`)**:
  - Count of interpreters (out of `r n_interp` in Round `r round_nr`) who assigned $m_{s, t^*, i} > 0$ to the best-candidate EFG:
```{r}
#| label: supporting-bullets
#| results: asis
for (i in seq_len(nrow(supp_summary))) {
    row <- supp_summary[i, ]
    unit_word <- ifelse(row$n_units == 1, "TASVEG unit", "TASVEG units")
    cat(sprintf(
        "    - `supporting = %d`: **%d %s** (`%s` pixels / `%s km²` / **%.2f%%** of mapped area)\n",
        row$supporting,
        row$n_units,
        unit_word,
        format(row$pixels, big.mark = ","),
        format(round(row$area_km2, 2), big.mark = ",", nsmall = 2),
        row$pct_area
    ))
}
```

---

## 5. Tabular Data Dictionaries

### `TASVEG-xref-best-candidate.csv` (`r nrow(xref_tbl)` rows × `r ncol(xref_tbl)` columns)

| Column | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `VEG_GROUP` | `string` | Broad TASVEG 5.0 vegetation group name (e.g., `Rainforest and related scrub`, `Dry eucalypt forest and woodland`). |
| `VEGCODE` | `string` | Three-letter TASVEG 5.0 mapping unit code (primary key, e.g., `AAP`, `WDA`). |
| `VEGCODE_D` | `string` | Full name/description of the TASVEG 5.0 community (e.g., `(AAP) Alkaline pans`). |
| `eligible` | `boolean` | `TRUE` for the `r n_eligible_units` cross-referenced vegetation communities; `FALSE` for `OAQ`, `ORO`, and `OSM` (which have `NA` in subsequent columns). |
| `EFG` | `string` | Best-candidate IUCN GET Level 3 Ecosystem Functional Group code (e.g., `TF1.7`, `T2.5`). |
| `efg_name` | `string` | Full name of the best-candidate EFG. |
| `efg_pixel_value` | `integer` | Integer value representing the EFG in `TASVEG-xref-target.tiff` (``r min(efg_lut$efg_pixel_value)`` to ``r max(efg_lut$efg_pixel_value)``). |
| `efg_hex_code` | `string` | Official hexadecimal color code (`#RRGGBB`) from the `geco` package. |
| `efg_rgb_code` | `string` | Comma-separated RGB triplet (`R,G,B`). |
| `round` | `integer` | Expert elicitation round (``r round_nr``). |
| `prop_memb` | `numeric` | Proportion of total Round `r round_nr` membership votes assigned to the best-candidate EFG (``r sprintf("%.2f", prop_min)`` to ``r sprintf("%.2f", prop_max)``). |
| `total_memb` | `numeric` | Total membership weight across all interpreters in Round `r round_nr` (``r n_interp``). |
| `supporting` | `integer` | Number of interpreters in Round `r round_nr` supporting the best-candidate EFG with membership $> 0$ (``r min(xref_elig$supporting)`` to ``r max(xref_elig$supporting)``). |
| `total_interp` | `integer` | Total number of interpreters assessing the unit in Round `r round_nr` (``r n_interp``). |

### `IUCN-GET-pixel-lookup.csv` (`r nrow(efg_lut)` rows × `r ncol(efg_lut)` columns)

| Column | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `efg_pixel_value` | `integer` | Integer pixel code in `TASVEG-xref-target.tiff` (``r min(efg_lut$efg_pixel_value)`` to ``r max(efg_lut$efg_pixel_value)``). |
| `EFG` | `string` | IUCN GET Level 3 code (e.g., `T2.3`). |
| `efg_name` | `string` | Full name of the Ecosystem Functional Group. |
| `realm_id` | `string` | IUCN GET Level 1 Realm code (`r paste(sprintf("\x60%s\x60", unique(efg_lut$realm_id)), collapse = ", ")`). |
| `realm_name` | `string` | IUCN GET Level 1 Realm name. |
| `biome_id` | `string` | IUCN GET Level 2 Functional Biome code (`r paste(sprintf("\x60%s\x60", unique(efg_lut$biome_id)), collapse = ", ")`). |
| `biome_name` | `string` | IUCN GET Level 2 Functional Biome name. |
| `efg_hex_code` | `string` | Hexadecimal color code (`#RRGGBB`). |
| `efg_rgb_code` | `string` | Comma-separated RGB color code (`R,G,B`). |
| `n_tasveg_units` | `integer` | Count of TASVEG 5.0 communities assigned to this EFG as their best candidate. |

---

## 6. How to Use This Dataset

### In QGIS or ArcGIS
- **QGIS:** Keep `TASVEG-xref-target.qml` in the same folder as `TASVEG-xref-target.tiff`. When you drag and drop `TASVEG-xref-target.tiff` into QGIS, it will automatically apply the official Global Ecosystems Atlas color palette and display both the EFG code and full name in the Layers legend.
- **ArcGIS Pro / GDAL:** Use `TASVEG-xref-target.clr` to import the color map and labels, or join `IUCN-GET-pixel-lookup.csv` on the `Value` = `efg_pixel_value` field.

### In R (`terra`)

```r
library(terra)
library(readr)

# 1. Load the three 90m rasters and lookup table
r_target <- rast("TASVEG-xref-target.tiff")
r_memb   <- rast("TASVEG-xref-membership.tiff")
r_supp   <- rast("TASVEG-xref-supporting.tiff")
lut      <- read_csv("IUCN-GET-pixel-lookup.csv")

# 2. Attach EFG labels as raster factor levels (categorical RAT)
levels(r_target) <- data.frame(
  id = lut$efg_pixel_value,
  EFG = lut$EFG,
  efg_name = lut$efg_name
)

plot(r_target, main = "Best-Candidate IUCN GET Ecosystem Functional Group (90 m)")

# 3. Example: Filter/mask to high-confidence areas (prop_memb >= 0.8 and supporting == 5)
high_conf_mask <- (r_memb >= 0.8) & (r_supp == 5)
r_target_high_conf <- mask(r_target, high_conf_mask, maskvalues = c(0, NA))
```

### In Python (`rasterio` / `pandas`)

```python
import pandas as pd
import rasterio

lut = pd.read_csv("IUCN-GET-pixel-lookup.csv")
xref = pd.read_csv("TASVEG-xref-best-candidate.csv")

with rasterio.open("TASVEG-xref-target.tiff") as src_targ, \
     rasterio.open("TASVEG-xref-membership.tiff") as src_memb:
    efg_arr = src_targ.read(1)
    memb_arr = src_memb.read(1)
    crs = src_targ.crs
    transform = src_targ.transform
```

### Reproducing the Outputs and Documentation from Source

These files are generated by [`inc/TASVEG-xref-IUCNGET-output-best-90m.R`](https://github.com/Ecosystem-Indicators-Workflows/TASVEG-XREF/blob/main/inc/TASVEG-xref-IUCNGET-output-best-90m.R) and [`output-best-candidate/README.qmd`](README.qmd) in the main workflow repository:

```bash
# 1. Download TASVEG 5.0 source shapefile into gisdata/
R --vanilla < scripts/TASVEG-data-download.R > docs-src/reproducibility-notes/TASVEG-data-download-out.txt

# 2. Run the synthesis and 90m GeoTIFF + CSV export
R --vanilla < scripts/TASVEG-xref-IUCNGET-output-best-90m.R > docs-src/reproducibility-notes/TASVEG-xref-IUCNGET-output-best-90m-out.txt

# 3. Re-render README.md with updated statistics from the generated files
quarto render output-best-candidate/README.qmd
```

**Required R packages:** `dplyr`, `readr`, `tidyr`, `stringr`, `foreach`, `terra`, `sf`, `fasterize`, `here`, `knitr`, `jsonlite`, plus GitHub packages `ecoSynthesis` and `Global-Ecosystems-Atlas/geco`.

title: 17  Overview of workflow outputs
text:
17.3 Derived single-EFG vector outputs
Using the parameterised script scripts/EFG-membership-vector.R (invoked with --args <EFG_CODE>), we can extract polygon-level GeoPackage datasets for individual Ecosystem Functional Groups of targeted conservation or Red List of Ecosystems interest, preserving all five individual interpreter membership columns alongside the aggregated synthesis metrics:



Parameterised workflow for single-EFG polygon vector extraction

scripts/EFG-membership-vector.R

## The purpose of this script is to create a spatial vector output (GeoPackage)
## for a single target Ecosystem Functional Group, including all TASVEG 5.0 polygons
## whose VEGCODE was assigned to the target by at least one interpreter in Round 2.
##
## Source classification and spatial data (units):
## > TASVEG 5.0 (vegetation communities)
## Target classification (unit):
## > IUCN Global Ecosystem Typology Level 3: provide EFG code, see example
## Output format:
## > GeoPackage (`TASVEG-xref-{EFG code}-memb.gpkg`) in `results/efg-{EFG code}-vector/`
## > plus a companion unit-level summary table (`TASVEG-xref-{EFG code}-unit-summary.csv`)
##
## Recommended usage (example  TF1.7 Boreal and temperate fens):
## R --vanilla --file="inc/EFG-membership-vector.R" --args TF1.7 > docs-src/reproducibility-notes/TF1.7-membership-vector-out.txt

## Step 0: Setup

### Benchmarking
start_time <- Sys.time()
date()

### Libraries
library(ecoSynthesis)
library(sf)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(readr)

### arguments

args <- commandArgs(trailingOnly = TRUE)
if (length(args) == 0) {
  stop("At least one argument must be supplied (target efg).n", call. = FALSE)
}
target_efg <- args[1]

### Paths
here::i_am("scripts/EFG-membership-vector.R")
load(here::here("results/XREFs/lookup-tables.rda"))
load(here::here("results/XREFs/memb-summaries.rda"))

out_dir <- here::here("results", sprintf("efg-%s-vector", target_efg))
if (!dir.exists(out_dir)) {
  dir.create(out_dir, recursive = TRUE)
}

## Step 1: Prepare individual interpreter and aggregated memberships for EFG

expert_initials <- c(
  "Anne Kitchener" = "memb_AK",
  "Adelina_Latinovic" = "memb_AL",
  "David_Keith" = "memb_DAK",
  "Jayne_Balmer" = "memb_JB",
  "Mark_Tozer" = "memb_MGT"
)

## Aggregated summary for EFG from Round 2 (all all assigned VEGCODEs)
efg_agg <- TASVEG_summary |>
  filter(EFG == target_efg) |>
  select(
    VEGCODE,
    EFG,
    round,
    prop_memb,
    total_memb,
    supporting,
    total_interp,
    best
  )

## Individual interpreter memberships for those VEGCODEs in Round 2
efg_interp_wide <- TASVEG_revised |>
  filter(EFG == target_efg, VEGCODE %in% efg_agg$VEGCODE) |>
  mutate(interp_col = expert_initials[expert]) |>
  select(VEGCODE, interp_col, memb) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = interp_col,
    values_from = memb,
    values_fill = 0
  )

## Ensure all 5 interpreter columns exist in consistent order
for (col_nm in unname(expert_initials)) {
  if (!(col_nm %in% colnames(efg_interp_wide))) {
    efg_interp_wide[[col_nm]] <- 0
  }
}

efg_table <- as_tibble(TASVEG) |>
  select(VEG_GROUP, VEGCODE, VEGCODE_D) |>
  inner_join(efg_agg, by = "VEGCODE") |>
  left_join(efg_interp_wide, by = "VEGCODE") |>
  select(
    VEG_GROUP,
    VEGCODE,
    VEGCODE_D,
    EFG,
    round,
    memb_AK,
    memb_AL,
    memb_DAK,
    memb_JB,
    memb_MGT,
    prop_memb,
    supporting,
    total_interp,
    best
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(prop_memb), VEGCODE)

# print(efg_table)

## Step 2: Filter TASVEG 5.0 polygons and join EFG attributes

TASVEG_xy <- read_sf(here::here(
  "gisdata/LIST_TASVEG_50_STATEWIDE",
  "TASVEG_5_0.shp"
))

TASVEG_efg_sf <- TASVEG_xy |>
  filter(VEGCODE %in% efg_table$VEGCODE) |>
  select(VEG_GROUP, VEGCODE, VEGCODE_D, SHAPE_LEN, SHAPE_AREA) |>
  left_join(
    efg_table |> select(-VEG_GROUP, -VEGCODE_D),
    by = "VEGCODE",
    relationship = "many-to-one"
  ) |>
  select(
    VEG_GROUP,
    VEGCODE,
    VEGCODE_D,
    EFG,
    round,
    memb_AK,
    memb_AL,
    memb_DAK,
    memb_JB,
    memb_MGT,
    prop_memb,
    supporting,
    total_interp,
    best,
    SHAPE_LEN,
    SHAPE_AREA
  )

cat(sprintf(
  "Selected %d polygons across %d VEGCODE units assigned to %s\n",
  nrow(TASVEG_efg_sf),
  n_distinct(TASVEG_efg_sf$VEGCODE),
  target_efg
))

## Step 3: Export GeoPackage vector and companion unit-level summary CSV

out_gpkg <- here::here(out_dir, sprintf("TASVEG-xref-%s-memb.gpkg", target_efg))
write_sf(
  TASVEG_efg_sf,
  dsn = out_gpkg,
  layer = "TASVEG_EFG_membership",
  delete_dsn = TRUE
)

poly_stats <- TASVEG_efg_sf |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  summarise(
    n_polygons = n(),
    unweighted_area_km2 = round(sum(SHAPE_AREA, na.rm = TRUE) / 1e6, 4),
    .by = VEGCODE
  )

efg_unit_summary <- efg_table |>
  left_join(poly_stats, by = "VEGCODE") |>
  mutate(
    weighted_area_prop_km2 = round(unweighted_area_km2 * prop_memb, 4),
    weighted_area_AK_km2 = round(unweighted_area_km2 * memb_AK, 4),
    weighted_area_AL_km2 = round(unweighted_area_km2 * memb_AL, 4),
    weighted_area_DAK_km2 = round(unweighted_area_km2 * memb_DAK, 4),
    weighted_area_JB_km2 = round(unweighted_area_km2 * memb_JB, 4),
    weighted_area_MGT_km2 = round(unweighted_area_km2 * memb_MGT, 4)
  )

write_csv(
  efg_unit_summary,
  here::here(out_dir, sprintf("TASVEG-xref-%s-unit-summary.csv", target_efg))

## 1. Overview & Methodology

This dataset provides a **polygon vector layer (`TASVEG-xref-TF1.7-memb.gpkg`)** and **unit-level summary table (`TASVEG-xref-TF1.7-unit-summary.csv`)** for **Level 3 Ecosystem Functional Group `TF1.7` (*Boreal and temperate fens*)** of the **IUCN Global Ecosystem Typology (IUCN GET)** in Tasmania, derived from **TASVEG 5.0**.

### Selection & Cross-Referencing Methodology

1. **Candidate Unit Filtering:**
   - Out of the 153 eligible vegetation community mapping units in **TASVEG 5.0**, **``r n_units`` vegetation communities (`VEGCODE`)** were assigned non-zero fuzzy membership ($\text{memb} > 0$) to **`TF1.7` (*Boreal and temperate fens*)** by at least one of the ``r n_interp`` domain experts in **Round ``r round_nr``** of structured expert elicitation.
   - All **``r format(n_polygons, big.mark = ",")`` polygons** belonging to these ``r n_units`` `VEGCODE` units were extracted from `TASVEG_5_0.shp` (total unweighted polygon area: **``r format(round(total_unweighted_km2, 2), big.mark = ",", nsmall = 2)`` $\text{km}^2$**).

2. **Individual Interpreter & Aggregated Membership Attributes:**
   - To preserve full transparency across interpreters, the polygon attribute table includes both:
     - **Individual interpreter fuzzy memberships** in Round ``r round_nr`` (`memb_AK`, `memb_AL`, `memb_DAK`, `memb_JB`, `memb_MGT`, each in $[0, 1]$), and
     - **Aggregated synthesis metrics** across all ``r n_interp`` interpreters:
       - `prop_memb`: Proportion of total Round ``r round_nr`` membership votes assigned to `TF1.7` ($\sum_{i=1}^{`r n_interp`} m_{s, \text{TF1.7}, i} / `r n_interp`$).
       - `supporting`: Number of interpreters (out of ``r n_interp``) assigning $>0$ membership to `TF1.7`.
       - `best`: Logical flag (`TRUE` / `FALSE`) indicating whether `TF1.7` is the single highest-scoring ("best") candidate EFG for that `VEGCODE` (`TRUE` for ``r best_unit_code``; `FALSE` for the remaining ``r n_units - n_best_units`` units where `TF1.7` represents a partial/secondary ecosystem component).

| Field Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `VEG_GROUP` | `string` | Broad TASVEG 5.0 vegetation group (`Highland treeless vegetation`, `Moorland, sedgeland and rushland`, `Saltmarsh and wetland`). |
| `VEGCODE` | `string` | Three-letter TASVEG 5.0 vegetation community code (`AAP`, `AHL`, `HCM`, `HSE`, `HSW`, `MGH`). |
| `VEGCODE_D` | `string` | Full name/description of the TASVEG 5.0 community. |
| `EFG` | `string` | Target IUCN GET Level 3 Ecosystem Functional Group code (`"TF1.7"`). |
| `round` | `integer` | Expert elicitation round (``r round_nr``). |
| `memb_AK` | `numeric` | Fuzzy membership assigned to `TF1.7` by interpreter **Anne Kitchener** ($[0, 1]$). |
| `memb_AL` | `numeric` | Fuzzy membership assigned to `TF1.7` by interpreter **Adelina Latinovic** ($[0, 1]$). |
| `memb_DAK` | `numeric` | Fuzzy membership assigned to `TF1.7` by interpreter **David A. Keith** ($[0, 1]$). |
| `memb_JB` | `numeric` | Fuzzy membership assigned to `TF1.7` by interpreter **Jayne Balmer** ($[0, 1]$). |
| `memb_MGT` | `numeric` | Fuzzy membership assigned to `TF1.7` by interpreter **Mark G. Tozer** ($[0, 1]$). |
| `prop_memb` | `numeric` | Aggregated proportion of total Round ``r round_nr`` membership votes across all ``r n_interp`` interpreters assigned to `TF1.7` ($[0.01, 0.94]$). |

## 6. How to Use This Dataset

### In QGIS
Keep `TASVEG-xref-TF1.7-memb.qml` in the same folder as `TASVEG-xref-TF1.7-memb.gpkg` (or load style via **Layer Properties → Symbology → Style → Load Style**).

### In R (`sf`)

```r
library(sf)
library(dplyr)

# 1. Read the GeoPackage
tf17_sf <- read_sf("TASVEG-xref-TF1.7-memb.gpkg")

# 2. Compute membership-weighted area (km2) by VEGCODE
tf17_sf |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  summarise(
    n_polygons = n(),
    unweighted_km2 = sum(SHAPE_AREA) / 1e6,
    weighted_km2   = sum(SHAPE_AREA * prop_memb) / 1e6,
    .by = c(VEGCODE, VEGCODE_D, prop_memb, supporting, best)
  )

# 3. Filter to polygons supported by at least 4 of 5 interpreters (AAP and MGH)
tf17_consensus <- tf17_sf |> filter(supporting >= 4)
```

### In Python (`geopandas`)

```python
import geopandas as gpd

gdf = gpd.read_file("TASVEG-xref-TF1.7-memb.gpkg")
gdf["weighted_area_km2"] = (gdf["SHAPE_AREA"] * gdf["prop_memb"]) / 1e6
print(gdf.groupby(["VEGCODE", "prop_memb", "supporting", "best"])["weighted_area_km2"].sum())
```

### Reproducing the Outputs from Source

```bash
# 1. Run the TF1.7 vector extraction and synthesis script
R --vanilla < scripts/TF1.7-membership-vector.R > docs-src/reproducibility-notes/TF1.7-membership-vector-out.txt

# 2. Render README.md with updated statistics
quarto render results/efg-TF1.7-vector/README.qmd --to gfm
```
